body.cap: Luxwagon's prototype compact hydroponic farming system | Photo provided by Luxwagon

body.x: Luxwagon Co., Ltd. (CEO Hyoseon Son) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas. At the K-Startup Pavilion, it will unveil its first hydroponic farming system.

Specializing in AI-powered solutions, Luxwagon has developed an innovative system designed to maximize agricultural productivity beyond the capabilities of traditional methods. Unlike conventional hydroponics, which are often limited to leafy greens, Luxwagon's technology is versatile enough to handle various crops, including vine-based plants. Its compact and efficient design enhances installation flexibility, making it adaptable to diverse environments.

Luxwagon’s hydroponic system leverages AI technology to optimize growing conditions, achieving up to 600 times the productivity of traditional open-field farming in an equivalent area. Compared to other hydroponic systems, it boasts up to 70 times greater efficiency per square meter. Its compact modular design allows operators to scale the growing area up or down based on their needs.

The system is versatile enough to support large-scale agricultural facilities such as plant factories and greenhouses while enabling small-scale farming in abandoned buildings or underutilized spaces. It’s particularly valuable in arid regions and water-scarce countries, offering a sustainable and resource-efficient farming solution.

body.cap: Projected plant factory using Luxwagon's hydroponic system | Photo provided by Luxwagon

body.x: Luxwagon has completed a prototype of its system and plans to showcase it for the first time at CES 2025, the world's largest IT and consumer electronics trade show. The company aims to increase visibility within the global smart farming industry while accelerating product development and commercialization.

A Luxwagon representative stated, “Due to climate change, agricultural environments are becoming increasingly uncertain, and countries and cities reliant on imported food are facing mounting challenges. Our solution, which produces diverse crops with minimal water usage, is expected to generate strong demand in these markets.”

The representative added, “We aim to introduce our hydroponic system to buyers from countries focused on securing sufficient and sustainable food resources. By engaging with stakeholders from the Middle East, China, and India at CES 2025, we hope to establish early market penetration and pave the way for commercialization.”
